newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down on caution over Wall St..
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down on caution over Wall St..

text.p: Mexican stocks edged down at the open on Friday in slow cautious trade as the market awaited further developments on the Dow Jones, traders said.
"It's very cautious, and obviously there's much pressure from the plunge on Wall Street, so we're waiting to see what happens there," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 1.85 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.05 percent, at 3,934.26.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile down 63.10 points to 7,267.08.
Trading volume of 31.6 million shares was vastly inflated by one single cross trade of 30.75 million shares.

Dealers said they had expected the Dow Jones to open strong when U.S. long bond yields dropped before the bell on mild revised first quarter GDP data. Nonetheless, the Dow fell on a worsened outlook for Intel Corp, they said.
Dealers expected the session to remain slow.
"There won't be much buying today, as funds closed their books yesterday," another trader said.
Traders noted the hefty cross trade that took up most volume was in financial group Bancomer A series, or controlling shares, rather than the more frequently traded B or common shares.
Sources at the Bancomer brokerage said the cross trade was settled in order to rearrange portfolios, rather than any chnage in shareholding control.
The trade came after an announcement on Thursday a new executive committee had been formed as part of the Bancomer group's management structure.
Telecomms firm Telmex L shares weighed most on the upside, gaining two centavos to 17.46, while holding company Femsa weighed most on the downside, off 45 centavos to 40.80 pesos.
Dealers said both stocks had traded at thin volume and did not necessarily reveal broader market trends.
On the broad market, of 34 stocks traded, eight were up while 13 were off.

Debt-ridden conglomerate Grupo Sidek topped the sliders' list, off one centavo to 75 centavos, minutes ahead of a shareholders' assembly. Stockwatchers said they would look to see whether Sidek announced a long-awaited debt restructuring plan.
